name: Spindle Cell Hemangioma
aliases: Spindle Cell Hemangioma of the Skin and Subcutis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Spindle Cell Hemangioma

criteria.description: Presence of spindle-shaped endothelial cells with cavernous vascular spaces on histological examination
Multiple or solitary nodules typically located in distal extremities, especially hands and feet
Positive staining for endothelial markers such as CD31 and CD34
Lack of cellular atypia, mitotic figures, and necrosis differentiating from malignant vascular tumors

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of spindle-shaped endothelial cells with cavernous vascular spaces plus clinical presentation of characteristic nodules
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on histopathology and immunohistochemical staining to differentiate from malignant vascular neoplasms.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multiple painless cutaneous or subcutaneous nodules
Spindle-shaped endothelial cell proliferation in lesion biopsy
searchTerms: spindle-shaped cells growing in lesion biopsy
abnormal cell growth in lesion sample

common.symptomName: Lesions predominantly located on distal extremities (hands and feet)
searchTerms: lesions mainly on hands and feet

common.symptomName: Slowly enlarging nodules over months to years
Occasional tenderness or discomfort at lesion site
searchTerms: occasional pain or tenderness at lesion

common.symptomName: Bluish to reddish discoloration of nodules
searchTerms: bluish to red colored skin nodules
discolored lumps ranging blue to red

occasional.symptomName: Limited range of motion if lesions near joints
searchTerms: limited range of motion due to nodules
enlarged lymph glands close to skin lesion

imaging: MRI showing well-circumscribed subcutaneous nodules with vascular characteristics
genetic: Some cases associated with mutations in IDH1/IDH2 genes
other: Histopathology revealing spindle cell proliferation and cavernous vascular spaces
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD31, CD34, and factor VIII-related antigen

distinguishingFeatures: Histology shows slit-like vascular spaces and spindle cells with atypia
Histology shows glomus cells rather than endothelial spindle cells
Histology shows lobular capillary proliferation without spindle cells

redFlags: Presence of systemic symptoms such as fever or weight loss
Histological evidence of cellular atypia or increased mitotic activity
references: Enzinger FM, Weiss SW. Soft Tissue Tumors. 6th ed. Elsevier; 2014.
Fetsch JF, et al. Spindle cell hemangioma: a clinicopathologic and immunohistochemical study of 78 cases. Am J Surg Pathol. 1996.
